analysis.title: UBS House View - Daily US: US equities can gain further after record highs
key_insights: The S&P 500 rose 0.6% on Tuesday to its first record high since August, bringing its year-to-date gain to 14.2%. The high came despite the ongoing Middle East conflict and US Treasury yields at multi-decade highs.
UBS expects the rally to continue despite periods of volatility, supported by AI investment, strong corporate earnings and solid economic growth.

Renewed strength in the AI trade supported the latest rally. Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 revenue forecast above Wall Street estimates and gave an upbeat long-term earnings outlook on demand for custom data center chips and other AI hardware. UBS says this points to continued AI compute and infrastructure demand, without taking a single-stock view.
UBS expects global AI-related capex to grow over 33% to USD 1.2tr in 2027. Consensus estimates project Nasdaq 100 earnings growth of 43% this year and 28% next year.
UBS estimates S&P 500 earnings growth of 25% this year and 14% in 2027. Growth is broadening beyond tech to consumer discretionary, financials, industrials, health care and utilities.
UBS forecasts US GDP growth of 2.2% this year and 2% in 2027. It expects the economy to withstand modest Fed policy tightening.

The US trade deficit widened in August to its largest since March 2025, a possible near-term drag on headline growth. UBS reads the robust imports as firm consumer demand and equipment investment, including AI-related capex.
Across 16 hiking cycles since 1954, the S&P 500 gained an average of 10.8% in the year after the first Fed hike. UBS argues earnings growth can offset valuation pressure from higher rates.

UBS forecasts the S&P 500 at 8,400 by June next year. It advises broadly diversified exposure across sectors and regions, and says investors can consider capital preservation strategies for more defensive positioning.

Health care: the Stoxx 600 Health Care index rose 0.6% on Tuesday, helped by positive late-stage lymphoma trial results. The sector still lags the market year to date. UBS views health care as attractive on reasonable valuations and structural growth drivers, with focus on obesity-market expansion, pipeline productivity, patent cliffs and Q3 earnings commentary.

sector_views.rationale: Remains a major contributor to S&P 500 earnings growth, supported by AI capex demand.
Resilient consumer spending should support earnings growth.
Robust capital market activity and a recovery in loan growth should benefit the sector.
Cyclical manufacturing improvement should lead to solid earnings growth.
Attractive on reasonable valuations, structural growth drivers such as aging populations, and relatively resilient earnings. Improving fundamentals in managed care and life sciences tools.
Liked for defensive characteristics and exposure to structural growth opportunities.

earnings_insights: Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 revenue forecast to above Wall Street estimates (company guidance, not a print) and gave an upbeat long-term earnings outlook on custom data center chip and AI hardware demand.
UBS estimate: S&P 500 earnings growth of 25% this year and 14% in 2027. Consensus estimate: Nasdaq 100 earnings growth of 43% this year and 28% next year.
Q3 earnings season in Europe and the US is the next test for health care: obesity-market expansion, pipeline productivity and patent-cliff plans.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient growth of 2.2% in 2026 and strong earnings growth (S&P 500 +25% this year, +14% in 2027) can offset valuation pressure, and the S&P 500 has averaged a 10.8% gain in the year after a first Fed hike.
tension_points.bear_case: US Treasury yields are at multi-decade highs, the Fed is expected to tighten modestly, and the widened August trade deficit could drag on headline growth.
